title: Docker Sandbox Kit Spec: Packaging AI Agent Permissions as OCI Images
key_facts: Docker announced on 24 Sep 2026 at WeAreDevelopers that it is bringing its Sandbox Kit Specification to the CNCF (Cloud Native Computing Foundation).
The Apache 2.0 spec, now at version 3, packages an AI agent, its tools and a typed list of the hosts, credentials and folders it requests into an ordinary OCI container image.
The aim is to make what an agent may access reviewable and portable, instead of living in shell history, dashboards and memory.
A Kit only requests permissions; the host decides. If a required request cannot be met, the launch is refused.
Docker Sandboxes, which run agents in microVMs, is the first and so far only runtime that supports the spec.
Docker says it built Kits with AWS, Box, Datadog, Dynatrace, JFrog, NanoClaw, OpenClaw, Palo Alto Networks and Snyk, among others; CNCF CTO Chris Aniszczyk welcomed the move.
The posts do not say whether the CNCF has accepted the spec into a program or at what maturity level.
quote_evidence: Docker has announced that it is bringing the Sandbox Kit Specification to the CNCF, aiming to make what an AI agent may access as portable as the agent itself.
The posts do not say whether the spec has been accepted into a CNCF program or which maturity level it would enter.

It is important to note that enforcement depends entirely on the runtime; since Docker Sandboxes is currently the only conforming implementation, portability across different runtimes has not yet been demonstrated.
why_it_matters_hint: A shared, reviewable way to describe what an AI agent may access could make agents easier to audit, but only one product supports it so far.
notes: Older news: the announcement was 24 Sep 2026, eight days before the window; InfoQ covered it on 2 Oct. Score lowered by 2. CNCF acceptance not confirmed in the article.
